title_en: Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is an inalienable part of the People's Republic of China.

Article 2 The National People's Congress authorizes the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to exercise a high degree of autonomy in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and to enjoy executive, legislative, independent judicial power, and the power of final adjudication.

Article 3 The executive authorities and legislature of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be composed of permanent residents of Hong Kong in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.
Article 4 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall safeguard the rights and freedoms of the residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and other persons in accordance with law.
Article 5 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall not practice the socialist system or policies and shall maintain the previous capitalist system and way of life for 50 years unchanged.
Article 6 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall protect the right to private property in accordance with law.

Article 7 The land and natural resources within the territory of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be state property. The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be responsible for their management, use, development, and for their lease or grant to individuals, legal persons, or organizations for use or development. The revenue derived therefrom shall be entirely at the disposal of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 8 The laws previously in force in Hong Kong, that is, the common law, rules of equity, ordinances, subordinate legislation, and customary law, shall be maintained, except for those which contravene this Law or which have been amended by the legislature of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 9 In addition to using Chinese, the executive authorities, legislature, and judiciary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may also use English, which shall be an official language as well.

Article 10 In addition to displaying the national flag and national emblem of the People's Republic of China, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may also display the regional flag and regional emblem of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The regional flag of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is a red flag with a bauhinia flower having five star-shaped stamens.
The regional emblem of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region has a bauhinia flower with five star-shaped stamens in the center, surrounded by the words "Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China" in Chinese and "Hong Kong" in English.

Article 11 In accordance with Article 31 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China, the systems and policies of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, including the social and economic systems, the system for safeguarding the fundamental rights and freedoms of its residents, the systems governing the executive, legislative, and judicial aspects, and the relevant policies, shall be based on the provisions of this Law.
No law enacted by the legislature of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall contravene this Law.

Article 12 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is a local administrative region of the People's Republic of China, which enjoys a high degree of autonomy and shall be directly under the Central People's Government.

Article 13 The Central People's Government shall be responsible for the foreign affairs relating to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China shall establish an office in Hong Kong to handle foreign affairs.
The Central People's Government authorizes the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to conduct relevant external affairs on its own in accordance with this Law.

Article 14 The Central People's Government shall be responsible for the defense of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be responsible for maintaining public order in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Military forces stationed by the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for defense shall not interfere with local affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, when necessary, ask the Central People's Government for assistance from the garrison in maintaining public order and in disaster relief. Personnel of the garrison shall, in addition to complying with national laws, comply with the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Expenditure for the garrison shall be borne by the Central People's Government.

Article 15 The Central People's Government shall appoint the Chief Executive and the principal officials of the executive authorities of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in accordance with the provisions of Chapter IV of this Law.

Article 16 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall enjoy executive power and shall, on its own, handle the administrative affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.

Article 17 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall enjoy legislative power. Laws enacted by the legislature of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record. The reporting for the record shall not affect the coming into force of such laws. If the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, after consulting the Committee for the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under it, considers that any law enacted by the legislature of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is not consistent with the provisions of this Law regarding affairs within the responsibility of the Central Authorities or regarding the relationship between the Central Authorities and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, it may return the law in question but shall not amend it. Any law returned by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall immediately cease to have effect. The cessation of effect of such a law shall have no retroactive effect, unless otherwise provided for in the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 18 The laws in force in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be this Law, the laws previously in force in Hong Kong as provided for in Article 8 of this Law, and laws enacted by the legislature of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. National laws shall not be applied in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region except for those listed in Annex III to this Law. The laws listed in Annex III to this Law shall be applied locally by way of promulgation or legislation by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may, after consulting the Committee for the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under it and the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, add to or delete from the list of laws in Annex III. Any law listed in Annex III shall be confined to those relating to defense, foreign affairs, and other matters which are not within the scope of the autonomy of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region as provided for by this Law. In the event that the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress decides to declare a state of war or decides that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is in a state of emergency due to the occurrence of turmoil within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region which endangers national unity or security and is beyond the control of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Central People's Government may issue an order applying the relevant national laws in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 19 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall enjoy independent judicial power and the power of final adjudication. The courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall have jurisdiction over all cases in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, subject to the restrictions previously existing in the legal system and principles of Hong Kong on the jurisdiction of the courts. The courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall have no jurisdiction over acts of state such as defense and foreign affairs. When trying cases, the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall obtain a certificate from the Chief Executive on questions of fact concerning acts of state such as defense and foreign affairs, which shall be binding on the courts. Before issuing such a certificate, the Chief Executive shall obtain a certifying document from the Central People's Government.

Article 20 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may enjoy other powers granted to it by the National People's Congress, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, or the Central People's Government.

Article 21 Chinese citizens who are residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, according to law, participate in the management of state affairs.
In accordance with the number of deputies and the method of their election determined by the National People's Congress, Chinese citizens who are residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, in Hong Kong, elect deputies of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to the National People's Congress to participate in the work of the highest organ of state power.

Article 22 No department of the Central People's Government and no province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government may interfere in the affairs which the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region administers on its own in accordance with this Law. If any department of the Central People's Government, or any province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government needs to set up an office in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, it shall obtain the consent of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the approval of the Central People's Government. All offices set up in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region by departments of the Central People's Government, provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, and their personnel, shall abide by the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. For entry into the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, persons from other parts of China shall apply for approval. The number of persons who enter the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for settlement shall be determined by the competent department of the Central People's Government after consulting the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may establish a representative office in Beijing.

Article 23 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall enact laws on its own to prohibit any act of treason, secession, sedition, subversion against the Central People's Government, or theft of state secrets, to prohibit foreign political organizations or bodies from conducting political activities in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and to prohibit political organizations or bodies of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region from establishing ties with foreign political organizations or bodies.
Article 25 All Hong Kong residents shall be equal before the law.
Article 26 Permanent residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall have the right to vote and the right to stand for election in accordance with law.

Article 27 Hong Kong residents shall have freedom of speech, of the press and of publication; freedom of association, of assembly, of procession and of demonstration; and the right and freedom to form and join trade unions, and to strike.

Article 28 The freedom of the person of Hong Kong residents shall be inviolable. No Hong Kong resident shall be subjected to arbitrary or unlawful arrest, detention or imprisonment. Arbitrary or unlawful search of the body of any resident or deprivation or restriction of the freedom of the person of any resident shall be prohibited. Torture of any resident or arbitrary or unlawful deprivation of the life of any resident shall be prohibited.
Article 29 The homes and other premises of Hong Kong residents shall be inviolable. Arbitrary or unlawful search of, or intrusion into, a resident's home or other premises shall be prohibited.

Article 30 The freedom and privacy of communication of Hong Kong residents shall be protected by law. No department or individual may, on any grounds, infringe upon the freedom and privacy of communication of residents except that the relevant authorities may inspect communications in accordance with legal procedures to meet the needs of public security or of investigation into criminal offences.

Article 31 Hong Kong residents shall have freedom of movement within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and freedom of emigration to other countries and regions. They shall have freedom to travel and to enter or leave the territory. Holders of valid travel documents may, unless restrained by law, leave the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region freely without special approval.

Article 32 Hong Kong residents shall have freedom of conscience.
Hong Kong residents shall have freedom of religious belief and freedom to preach and to conduct and participate in religious activities in public.
Article 33 Hong Kong residents shall have freedom of choice of occupation.
Article 34 Hong Kong residents shall have freedom to engage in academic research, literary and artistic creation, and other cultural activities.

Article 35 Hong Kong residents shall have the right to confidential legal advice, access to the courts, choice of lawyers for timely protection of their lawful rights and interests or for representation in court, and to judicial remedies.
Hong Kong residents shall have the right to institute legal proceedings in the courts against the acts of the executive departments and their personnel.
Article 36 Hong Kong residents shall have the right to enjoy social welfare in accordance with law. The welfare benefits and retirement security of the working class shall be protected by law.
Article 37 The freedom of marriage of Hong Kong residents and their right to bear children voluntarily shall be protected by law.
Article 38 Hong Kong residents shall enjoy the other rights and freedoms safeguarded by the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 39 The provisions of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, and international labour conventions as applied to Hong Kong shall remain in force and shall be implemented through the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The rights and freedoms enjoyed by Hong Kong residents shall not be restricted unless as prescribed by law. Such restrictions shall not contravene the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article.
Article 40 The lawful traditional rights and interests of the indigenous inhabitants of the "New Territories" shall be protected by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 41 Persons other than Hong Kong residents within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, according to law, enjoy the rights and freedoms of Hong Kong residents prescribed in this Chapter.
Article 42 Hong Kong residents and other persons in Hong Kong shall have the obligation to abide by the laws in force in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 43 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be the head of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and shall represent the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be accountable to the Central People's Government and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 44 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be a Chinese citizen who has reached the age of 40 years, has ordinarily resided in Hong Kong for a continuous period of not less than 20 years and has no right of abode in any foreign country, and who is a permanent resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 45 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be selected by election or through consultations held in the Region and be appointed by the Central People's Government.
The method for selecting the Chief Executive shall be specified in the light of the actual situation in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and in accordance with the principle of gradual and orderly progress. The ultimate aim shall be the selection of the Chief Executive by universal suffrage upon nomination by a broadly representative nominating committee in accordance with democratic procedures.
The specific method for selecting the Chief Executive shall be prescribed by Annex I: Method for the Selection of the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Article 46 The term of office of the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be five years. The Chief Executive may serve for a second term.

Article 47 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be dedicated to his or her duties and shall be honest in performing his or her functions.
Upon assuming office, the Chief Executive shall declare his or her assets to the Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and record such declaration.

Article 49 If the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region considers that a bill passed by the Legislative Council is not compatible with the overall interests of the Region, the Chief Executive may return the bill to the Legislative Council within three months for reconsideration. If the Legislative Council passes the original bill again by a two-thirds majority of all its members, the Chief Executive shall sign and promulgate it within one month, or deal with it in accordance with the provisions of Article 50 of this Law.

Article 50 If the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region refuses to sign a bill returned by the Legislative Council for the second time, or if the Legislative Council refuses to pass a budget or any other important bill introduced by the Government, and if after consultation consensus still cannot be reached, the Chief Executive may dissolve the Legislative Council.
Before dissolving the Legislative Council, the Chief Executive shall obtain the consent of the Executive Council. The Chief Executive may dissolve the Legislative Council only once in each term of his or her office.

Article 51 If the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region refuses to approve the budget introduced by the Government, the Chief Executive may apply to the Legislative Council for provisional appropriations. If the Legislative Council is dissolved and cannot approve the budget, the Chief Executive may approve provisional short-term appropriations for a period before the election of the new Legislative Council, in accordance with the expenditure level of the previous fiscal year.

Article 53 If the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is unable to discharge his or her duties for a short period, such duties shall be temporarily assumed by the Secretary for Home Affairs, the Financial Secretary and the Secretary for Justice in that order.
In the event that the office of the Chief Executive becomes vacant, a new Chief Executive shall be selected within six months in accordance with the provisions of Article 45 of this Law. During the vacancy, the acting duties of the Chief Executive shall be assumed in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
Article 54 The Executive Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be an organ for assisting the Chief Executive in policy-making.

Article 55 The members of the Executive Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be appointed by the Chief Executive from among the principal officials of the executive authorities, members of the Legislative Council and public figures. Their appointment or removal shall be decided by the Chief Executive. The term of office of a member of the Executive Council shall not extend beyond the term of office of the Chief Executive who appointed him or her.
Members of the Executive Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be Chinese citizens who are permanent residents of the Region and have no right of abode in any foreign country.
The Chief Executive may, when necessary, invite relevant persons to attend Executive Council meetings.

Article 56 The Executive Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be presided over by the Chief Executive.
Before making important policy decisions, introducing bills to the Legislative Council, making subordinate legislation, or dissolving the Legislative Council, the Chief Executive shall consult the Executive Council, except in matters concerning the appointment and removal of personnel, disciplinary sanctions, or measures taken in emergencies.
If the Chief Executive does not accept the advice of a majority of the members of the Executive Council, the Chief Executive shall record the specific reasons therefor.

Article 57 A Commission Against Corruption shall be established in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Commission shall function independently and shall be accountable to the Chief Executive.
Article 58 A Commission of Audit shall be established in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Commission shall function independently and shall be accountable to the Chief Executive.
Article 59 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be the executive authorities of the Region.

Article 60 The head of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be the Chief Executive of the Region.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall comprise the Department of Home Affairs, the Department of Finance, the Department of Justice, and various bureaux, divisions and commissions.

Article 61 The principal officials of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be Chinese citizens who are permanent residents of the Region, have ordinarily resided in Hong Kong for a continuous period of not less than 15 years and have no right of abode in any foreign country.
Article 63 The Department of Justice of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall control criminal prosecutions, free from any interference.

Article 64 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region must abide by the law and be accountable to the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region: it shall implement laws passed by the Council and already in force; it shall present regular policy addresses to the Council; it shall answer questions raised by members of the Council; and the approval of the Legislative Council shall be required for taxation and public expenditure.
Article 65 The system previously operated by the executive authorities for establishing advisory bodies shall be maintained.
Article 66 The Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be the legislature of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 67 The Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be composed of Chinese citizens who are permanent residents of the Region with no right of abode in any foreign country. However, permanent residents of the Region who are not of Chinese nationality or who have the right of abode in foreign countries may also be elected as members of the Legislative Council of the Region, provided that the proportion of such members shall not exceed 20 percent of the total membership of the Council.

Article 68 The Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be constituted by election.
The method for forming the Legislative Council shall be specified in the light of the actual situation in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and in accordance with the principle of gradual and orderly progress. The ultimate aim shall be the election of all members of the Legislative Council by universal suffrage.
The specific method for forming the Legislative Council and its procedures for voting on bills and motions shall be prescribed by Annex II: "Method for the Formation of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and Its Voting Procedures".
Article 69 The term of office of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be four years, except the first term which shall be two years.

Article 70 If the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is dissolved by the Chief Executive in accordance with the provisions of this Law, it shall be reconstituted by election within three months in accordance with the provisions of Article 68 of this Law.

Article 71 The President of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be elected by and from among the members of the Legislative Council.
The President of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be a Chinese citizen who is a permanent resident of the Region, has ordinarily resided in Hong Kong for a continuous period of not less than 20 years, has attained the age of 40 years, and has no right of abode in any foreign country.

Article 74 Members of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may introduce bills in accordance with the provisions of this Law and legal procedures. Bills which do not relate to public expenditure, the political structure or the operation of the government may be introduced individually or jointly by members of the Legislative Council. The written consent of the Chief Executive shall be required before bills relating to government policies are introduced.

Article 75 The quorum for the meeting of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be not less than one half of all its members.
The rules of procedure of the Legislative Council shall be made by the Council itself, provided that they shall not be inconsistent with this Law.
Article 76 A bill passed by the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may take effect only after it has been signed and promulgated by the Chief Executive.
Article 77 Members of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be immune from legal proceedings in respect of their statements at meetings of the Council.

Article 78 Members of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be immune from arrest when attending meetings of the Council or on their way to and from such meetings.
Article 80 The courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region at all levels shall be the judiciary of the Region, exercising the judicial power of the Region.

Article 81 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall establish the Court of Final Appeal, the High Court, the District Courts, the Magistrates' Courts and other special courts. The High Court shall consist of the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance.
The judicial system previously in force in Hong Kong shall be maintained, except for whatever changes consequent upon the establishment of the Court of Final Appeal of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 82 The power of final adjudication of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be vested in the Court of Final Appeal of the Region. The Court of Final Appeal may, as required, invite judges from other common law jurisdictions to participate in the adjudication of cases.
The organization and powers of the courts at all levels of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be prescribed by law.

The courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall adjudicate cases in accordance with the laws applicable to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region as specified in Article 18 of this Law, and judicial precedents from other common law jurisdictions may be referred to as reference.

The courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall exercise judicial power independently, free from any interference. Judicial personnel shall not be subject to legal liability for their acts in the performance of their adjudicative functions.
The principles of the jury system previously practiced in Hong Kong shall be maintained.

In criminal and civil actions in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the principles previously applicable in Hong Kong and the rights of parties shall be maintained.
Any person who is lawfully arrested shall have the right to a fair trial by the judicial organs without delay and shall be presumed innocent until convicted by the judicial organs.

Judges of the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be appointed by the Chief Executive on the recommendation of an independent commission composed of local judges, legal professionals, and other eminent persons.

A judge of a court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may only be removed from office by the Chief Executive on the recommendation of a tribunal appointed by the Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal and consisting of not less than three local judges, for inability to discharge his or her duties or for misbehavior.
The Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may only be removed from office by the Chief Executive on the recommendation of a tribunal consisting of not less than five local judges appointed for the purpose of investigation, and in accordance with the procedures prescribed by this Law, for inability to discharge his or her duties or for misbehavior.

The Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal and the Chief Judge of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be Chinese citizens who are permanent residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region with no right of abode in any foreign country.
In addition to the procedures prescribed in Articles 88 and 89 of this Law, the appointment or removal of judges of the Court of Final Appeal and the Chief Judge of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall also be subject to the consent of the Legislative Council obtained by the Chief Executive and shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record.
The original system for appointment and removal of judicial personnel other than judges in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be maintained.

Judges and other judicial personnel of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be selected on the basis of their judicial and professional qualities and may be recruited from other common law jurisdictions.

Judges and other judicial personnel who served in Hong Kong before the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may all remain in employment, and their length of service shall be retained. Their salaries, allowances, benefits and terms and conditions of service shall not be less favorable than the original standards.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall pay, in accordance with standards not lower than the original ones, the pensions, gratuities, allowances and benefits due to retired or otherwise discharged judges and other judicial personnel, including those who have retired or been discharged before the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, or to their families, irrespective of their nationality or place of residence.

The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, by reference to the previous practice in Hong Kong, make provisions concerning the work and practice of local and overseas lawyers in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, through consultations and in accordance with law, maintain judicial liaison and render mutual assistance with the judicial organs of other parts of the country.

With the assistance or authorization of the Central People's Government, the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may make appropriate arrangements with foreign states for reciprocal judicial assistance.

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may establish non-administrative regional organizations to receive the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region's advice on matters such as district administration and other affairs, or to be responsible for providing services such as culture, recreation, and environmental sanitation.
The powers and methods of composition of regional organizations shall be prescribed by law.

Public servants serving in all government departments of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region must be permanent residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. This provision shall not apply to foreign public servants otherwise provided for in Article 101 of this Law or to those below a certain rank as prescribed by law.
Public servants must be dedicated to their duties and be responsible to the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Public servants who served in the government departments of Hong Kong, including the police department, before the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may all remain in employment, and their length of service shall be retained. Their salaries, allowances, benefits and terms and conditions of service shall not be less favorable than the original standards.

The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may employ British or other foreign nationals who were formerly public servants in Hong Kong or who hold permanent identity cards of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region as public servants in government departments at all levels, but the following officials must be Chinese citizens who are permanent residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region with no right of abode in any foreign country: Secretaries of Departments, Deputy Secretaries of Departments, Directors of Bureaux, Commissioner Against Corruption, Director of Audit, Commissioner of Police, Director of Immigration, and Commissioner of Customs and Excise.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may also employ British and other foreign nationals as advisers to government departments, and when necessary, may recruit qualified persons from outside the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to serve as specialists and technical personnel in government departments. Such foreign nationals shall be employed only in their individual capacities and shall be responsible to the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall pay, in accordance with standards not lower than the original ones, the pensions, gratuities, allowances and benefits due to retired or otherwise discharged public servants, including those who have retired or been discharged before the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, or to their families, irrespective of their nationality or place of residence.

Article 103 Public servants shall be appointed and promoted on the basis of their qualifications, experience and ability. Hong Kong's previous system of recruitment, employment, assessment, discipline, training and management for the public service, including special bodies responsible for the appointment, pay and conditions of service of public servants, shall be maintained, except for any provisions relating to privileged treatment of foreign nationals.

Article 104 When assuming office, the Chief Executive, principal officials, members of the Executive Council and of the Legislative Council, judges of the courts at all levels and other members of the judiciary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region must, in accordance with law, swear allegiance to the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China and pledge loyalty to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

Article 105 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, protect the right of individuals and legal persons to the acquisition, use, disposal and inheritance of property and their right to compensation for lawful deprivation of their property.
Such compensation shall correspond to the real value of the property concerned at the time and shall be freely convertible and paid without delay.
The ownership of enterprises and the investments from outside the Region shall be protected by law.

Article 106 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall maintain independent finances.
All revenues of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be used for its own needs and shall not be handed over to the Central People's Government.
The Central People's Government shall not levy taxes in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 107 The fiscal budget of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be based on the principle of keeping expenditure within the limits of revenues, strive to achieve a fiscal balance, avoid deficits, and be commensurate with the growth rate of its gross domestic product.

Article 108 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall have an independent taxation system.
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, taking the low tax policy previously implemented in Hong Kong as reference, enact laws on its own concerning the types of taxes, tax rates, tax reductions, allowances and exemptions, and other matters of taxation.

Article 109 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall provide an appropriate economic and legal environment for maintaining the status of Hong Kong as an international financial centre.

Article 110 The monetary and financial systems of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be prescribed by law.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate monetary and financial policies, safeguard the freedom of operation of financial enterprises and financial markets, and regulate and supervise them in accordance with law.

Article 111 The Hong Kong dollar, as the legal tender of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, shall continue to circulate.
The power of issuing Hong Kong dollars shall be vested in the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The issue of Hong Kong dollars shall be backed by a 100 per cent reserve fund. The system regarding the issue of Hong Kong dollars and the reserve fund system shall be prescribed by law.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may authorize designated banks to issue or to continue to issue Hong Kong dollars under statutory authority, after satisfying itself that any issue of Hong Kong dollars is soundly based and that the arrangements for such issue are consistent with the objective of maintaining the stability of the Hong Kong dollar.

Article 112 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall not impose foreign exchange control policies. The Hong Kong dollar shall be freely convertible. Markets for foreign exchange, gold, securities, futures and the like shall continue to be open.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall safeguard the free flow of capital within, into and out of the Region.

Article 113 The Exchange Fund of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be managed and controlled by the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, primarily for regulating the exchange value of the Hong Kong dollar.
Article 114 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall maintain the status of a free port and shall not impose any customs duty except where otherwise provided by law.
Article 115 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall pursue a policy of free trade and safeguard the free movement of goods, intangible property and capital.

Article 116 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be a separate customs territory.
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, using the name 'Hong Kong, China', participate in relevant international organizations and international trade agreements (including preferential trade arrangements), such as the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and arrangements regarding international trade in textiles.
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall enjoy the export quotas, tariff preferences and other similar arrangements obtained or previously obtained and still valid, all of which shall be exclusively enjoyed by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Article 117 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may issue certificates of origin for products in accordance with prevailing rules of origin.

Article 118 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall provide an economic and legal environment for encouraging investments, technological progress and the development of new industries.

Article 119 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall formulate appropriate policies to promote and co-ordinate the development of various trades such as manufacturing, commerce, tourism, real estate, transport, public utilities, services, agriculture and fisheries, and pay attention to environmental protection.

Article 120 All leases of land granted, decided upon or renewed before the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region which extend beyond 30 June 1997, and all rights in relation to such leases, shall continue to be recognized and protected under the law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 121 As regards all leases of land granted between 27 May 1985 and 30 June 1997 which extend beyond 30 June 1997 and do not exceed 30 June 2047, or which were renewed without a right of renewal and extend beyond 30 June 1997 but do not exceed 30 June 2047, the lessee shall not pay an additional premium from 1 July 1997, but shall pay an annual rent equivalent to three per cent of the rateable value of the property at that date. Thereafter, the rent shall be adjusted in line with any changes in the rateable value.

Article 122 In the case of old schedule lots, village lots, small houses and similar rural holdings, where the lessee on 30 June 1984, or, in the case of small houses granted after that date, the lessee, is a person descended through the male line from a person who was in 1898 a resident of an established village in Hong Kong, the original rent shall remain unchanged so long as the lessee remains that person or his lawful successor in the male line.

Article 123 With regard to land leases that expire after the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region but without a right of renewal, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own laws and policies for their handling.

Article 124 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall maintain the shipping operation and management systems previously in operation in Hong Kong, including the system for the management of seafarers.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, prescribe its specific functions and responsibilities in respect of shipping.

Article 125 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, upon authorization by the Central People's Government, continue to undertake ship registration and, in accordance with the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, issue relevant certificates under the name "Hong Kong, China".

Article 126 Except for foreign military vessels, which require special permission from the Central People's Government to enter the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, other vessels may enter and leave its ports in accordance with the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Article 127 Private shipping and shipping-related enterprises and private container terminals in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may continue to operate freely.
Article 128 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall provide conditions and take measures to maintain Hong Kong's status as an international and regional aviation center.

Article 129 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall continue to implement the civil aviation management system previously in operation in Hong Kong and, in accordance with the regulations of the Central People's Government concerning aircraft nationality marks and registration marks, shall set up its own aircraft register.
Foreign state aircraft entering the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall require special permission from the Central People's Government.

Article 130 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be responsible on its own for the daily operation and technical management of civil aviation, including the management of airports, the provision of air traffic services within the flight information region of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and the performance of other duties prescribed by the regional navigation procedures of the International Civil Aviation Organization.

Article 131 The Central People's Government shall, after consultation with the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, make arrangements to provide airlines registered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and having Hong Kong as their principal place of business, and other airlines of the People's Republic of China, with scheduled flights between the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and other areas of the People's Republic of China.

Article 132 Civil air transport agreements involving flights between other areas of the People's Republic of China and other countries or regions with a stopover in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and flights between the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and other countries or regions with a stopover in other areas of the People's Republic of China, shall be concluded by the Central People's Government.
When concluding the civil air transport agreements referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, the Central People's Government shall take into account the special circumstances and economic interests of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and shall consult with the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
When the Central People's Government negotiates with foreign governments regarding the arrangements for flights referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, representatives of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may participate as members of the delegation of the Government of the People's Republic of China.

Article 133 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, with specific authorization from the Central People's Government:
(1) renew or amend existing civil air transport agreements and arrangements;
(2) negotiate and conclude new civil air transport agreements providing routes for airlines registered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and having Hong Kong as their principal place of business, and rights for overflights and technical stops; and
(3) negotiate and conclude provisional agreements with foreign countries or regions with which no civil air transport agreement has been concluded.
Scheduled flights that do not involve a journey to, from or through the Mainland of China but solely to, from or through Hong Kong shall be regulated by the civil air transport agreements or provisional agreements referred to in this Article.

Article 135 Airlines registered in Hong Kong and having Hong Kong as their principal place of business before the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and businesses related to civil aviation, may continue to operate.

Article 136 On the basis of the previous educational system, the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate policies on the development and improvement of education, including policies regarding the educational system and its administration, the language of instruction, the allocation of funds, the examination system, the system of academic awards and the recognition of educational qualifications.
Community organizations and individuals may, according to law, run various educational undertakings in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 137 Educational institutions of all kinds may retain their autonomy and enjoy academic freedom. They may continue to recruit staff and use teaching materials from outside the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Schools run by religious organizations may continue to provide religious education, including courses in religion. Students shall enjoy freedom of choice of educational institutions and freedom to pursue their education outside the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 138 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate policies on the development of Chinese and Western medicine and on the improvement of medical and health services. Community organizations and individuals may, according to law, provide various medical and health services.

Article 139 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate policies on science and technology and shall, by law, protect the achievements in scientific and technological research, patents and inventions and creations.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, determine the scientific and technological standards and specifications applicable to Hong Kong.

Article 140 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate policies on culture and shall, by law, protect the achievements and the lawful rights and interests of authors in their literary and artistic creation.

Article 141 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall not restrict the freedom of religious belief, shall not interfere in the internal affairs of religious organizations, and shall not restrict religious activities which do not contravene the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Religious organizations shall, according to law, enjoy the rights to acquire, use, dispose of and inherit property and the right to receive financial assistance. Their previous property rights and interests shall be maintained and protected. Religious organizations may, according to their previous methods, continue to run seminaries and other schools, hospitals and welfare institutions and to provide other social services. Religious organizations and believers in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may maintain and develop relations with religious organizations and believers elsewhere.

Article 142 On the basis of maintaining the previous professional system, the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate provisions on the assessment of the qualifications for practice in the various professions.
Persons who have obtained professional and practicing qualifications before the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may retain their previous qualifications in accordance with the relevant regulations and professional codes.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall continue to recognize the professions and the professional organizations recognized prior to the establishment of the Special Administrative Region, and professional organizations so recognized may, on their own, assess and confer professional qualifications.
The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, in light of the needs of social development and after consulting the views of the relevant parties, recognize new professions and professional organizations.

Article 143 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate policies on sports. Non-governmental sports organizations may, according to law, continue to exist and develop.

Article 144 The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall maintain the policy previously in force in Hong Kong in respect of subventions for non-governmental organizations in fields such as education, medical and health services, culture, the arts, recreation, sports, social welfare and social work. Staff members previously serving in subvented organizations in Hong Kong may, in accordance with the previous system, remain in their employment.

Article 145 On the basis of the previous social welfare system, the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate policies on the development and improvement of this system in light of the economic conditions and social needs.

Article 146 Voluntary organizations providing social services in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, on their own, decide their modes of service, provided that the law is not contravened.
Article 147 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate laws and policies on labor.

Article 148 The relationship between non-governmental organizations and religious organizations in fields such as education, science, technology, culture, the arts, sports, the professions, medical and health services, labor, social welfare and social work in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and their counterparts on the mainland shall be based on the principles of non-subordination, non-interference and mutual respect.

Article 149 Non-governmental organizations and religious organizations in fields such as education, science, technology, culture, the arts, sports, the professions, medical and health services, labor, social welfare and social work in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may maintain and develop relations with their counterparts in other countries and regions and with relevant international organizations. They may, as required, use the name “Hong Kong, China” to participate in such activities.

Article 150 Representatives of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, as members of a delegation of the Government of the People's Republic of China, participate in diplomatic negotiations conducted by the Central People's Government which are directly related to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 151 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, using the name “Hong Kong, China”, on its own, maintain and develop relations and conclude and implement agreements with other countries and regions and relevant international organizations in such fields as the economy, trade, finance, shipping, communications, tourism, culture and sports.

Article 152 In respect of international organizations and international conferences in the appropriate fields to which states are parties and which are related to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may send representatives to participate as members of a delegation of the People's Republic of China, or may participate in such capacity as may be permitted by the Central People's Government and the international organization or international conference concerned, and may express their views in the name of “Hong Kong, China”.
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, using the name “Hong Kong, China”, participate in international organizations and international conferences not limited to states.
For international organizations in which the People's Republic of China is a member and in which Hong Kong has also participated in some form, the Central People's Government shall take the necessary measures to enable the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to continue to maintain its status in such organizations in an appropriate form.
For international organizations in which the People's Republic of China is not a member but in which Hong Kong has participated in some form, the Central People's Government shall, as necessary, enable the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to continue to participate in such organizations in an appropriate form.

Article 153 The Central People's Government may, in light of the circumstances and needs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and after consulting the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, decide whether any international agreement concluded by the People's Republic of China shall apply to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. International agreements to which the People's Republic of China is not a party but which have previously been applied to Hong Kong may continue to apply. The Central People's Government shall, as necessary, authorize or assist the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to make appropriate arrangements for the application to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of other relevant international agreements.

Article 154 The Central People's Government authorizes the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government to, in accordance with law, issue passports of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China to Chinese citizens who hold permanent identity cards of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and to issue other travel documents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China to other persons lawfully residing in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The above passports and documents shall be valid for all countries and regions and shall certify the holder's right to return to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government may implement immigration controls with respect to the entry, stay, and departure of persons from all countries and regions.

Article 155 The Central People's Government shall assist or authorize the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to conclude visa abolition agreements with various states or regions.

Article 156 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may, as necessary, establish official or semi-official economic and trade offices in foreign countries and shall report to the Central People's Government for the record.

Article 157 Foreign consular institutions or other official or semi-official institutions established in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall obtain approval from the Central People's Government.
Consular institutions and other official institutions established in Hong Kong by countries that have established formal diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China may be retained.
Consular institutions and other official institutions established in Hong Kong by countries that have not yet established formal diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China may, depending on the circumstances, be allowed to be retained or changed to semi-official institutions.
Countries not yet recognized by the People's Republic of China may only establish non-governmental institutions in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 158 The power of interpretation of this Law shall be vested in the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall authorize the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to interpret on their own, in adjudicating cases, the provisions of this Law which are within the limits of the autonomy of the Region.
The courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region may also interpret other provisions of this Law in adjudicating cases. However, if the courts of the Region, in adjudicating cases, need to interpret the provisions of this Law concerning affairs which are the responsibility of the Central People's Government or concerning the relationship between the Central Authorities and the Region, and if such interpretation affects the judgments in the cases, the courts of the Region shall, before making their final judgments which are not appealable, seek an interpretation of the relevant provisions from the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress through the Court of Final Appeal of the Region. When the Standing Committee makes an interpretation, the courts of the Region, in applying those provisions, shall follow the interpretation of the Standing Committee. However, judgments previously rendered shall not be affected.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall consult its Committee for the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region before giving an interpretation of this Law.

Article 159 The power to amend this Law shall belong to the National People's Congress.
The power to propose amendments to this Law shall belong to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the State Council and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. An amendment proposal from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be submitted to the National People's Congress by the delegation of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to the National People's Congress after obtaining the consent of two-thirds majority of the deputies to the National People's Congress from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, two-thirds majority of all members of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Before an amendment proposal for this Law is placed on the agenda of the National People's Congress, the Committee for the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall study it and submit its opinions.
No amendment to this Law shall contravene the established basic policies of the People's Republic of China regarding Hong Kong.

Article 160 Upon the establishment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the laws previously in force in Hong Kong shall be adopted as laws of the Region except for those which the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress declares to be in contravention of this Law. If any subsequent laws are found to be in contravention of this Law, they may be amended or cease to have effect in accordance with the procedures prescribed by this Law.
Documents, certificates, contracts, and rights and obligations valid under the laws previously in force in Hong Kong shall continue to be valid and shall be recognized and protected by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, provided that they do not contravene this Law.
Annex I
Method for the Selection of the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
1. The Chief Executive shall be selected by an Election Committee which is broadly representative and shall be appointed by the Central People's Government in accordance with this Law.
2. The Election Committee shall be composed of 800 members from the following sectors:
The term of office of the Election Committee shall be five years.
3. The delimitation of the various sectors, the organizations in each sector which may elect members of the Election Committee, and the number of such members shall be prescribed by an electoral law enacted by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in accordance with the principles of democracy and openness.
The statutory bodies in the various sectors shall, in accordance with the allocation of members and the electoral methods prescribed by the electoral law, elect the members of the Election Committee on their own.
Members of the Election Committee shall vote in their individual capacities.
4. Candidates for the office of Chief Executive may be jointly nominated by not less than 100 members of the Election Committee. Each member may nominate only one candidate.
5. The Election Committee shall, on the basis of the list of nominees, elect the person to be designated as the Chief Executive by secret ballot on a one-person-one-vote basis. The specific method of election shall be prescribed by the electoral law.
6. The first Chief Executive shall be selected in accordance with the "Decision of the National People's Congress on the Method for the Formation of the First Government and the First Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region."
7. If the method for selecting the Chief Executive for terms subsequent to the year 2007 needs to be amended, it shall be passed by a two-thirds majority of all the members of the Legislative Council and consented to by the Chief Executive, and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for approval.
Annex II
Method for the Formation of the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and Its Voting Procedures
I. Method for the Formation of the Legislative Council
(1) The Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be composed of 60 members in each term. The first Legislative Council shall be formed in accordance with the "Decision of the National People's Congress on the Method for the Formation of the First Government and the First Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region." The compositions of the second and third Legislative Councils shall be as follows:

(2) Except for the first Legislative Council, the Election Committee referred to above is the one prescribed in Annex I to this Law. The delineation of geographical constituencies for direct election, the voting method, the delimitation of functional sectors and statutory bodies, the distribution of seats for members of the Legislative Council, the electoral method, and the method for the Election Committee to elect members of the Legislative Council shall be prescribed by an electoral law proposed by the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and passed by the Legislative Council.
II. Voting Procedure of the Legislative Council on Bills and Motions
Unless otherwise provided for in this Law, the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall adopt the following procedure for voting on bills and motions:
Bills introduced by the government shall require a simple majority of the members of the Legislative Council present for passage.
Motions, bills, and amendments to government bills introduced by individual members of the Legislative Council shall require a simple majority of the members present from each of the two groups: (a) members returned by functional constituencies, and (b) members returned by geographical constituencies and by the Election Committee.
III. Method for the Formation of the Legislative Council and Its Voting Procedures for Terms Subsequent to the Year 2007
If the method for forming the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the voting procedures for bills and motions for terms subsequent to the year 2007 need to amend the provisions of this Annex, such amendments shall be passed by a two-thirds majority of all the members of the Legislative Council, consented to by the Chief Executive, and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record.
Annex III

The following national laws shall be applied locally by way of promulgation or legislation by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region with effect from July 1, 1997:

4. Statement of the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Territorial Sea
5. Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China
6. Regulations of the People's Republic of China Concerning Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities
